title: Implicit Church-faith alone insufficient; explicit Creed articles required for salvation
source_text: XXVII. Ultro quoque concedunt ad salutem non sufficere, ut aliquis generatim & implicite credat quod Ecclesia credit, etiamsi nullius mysteriorum divinorum expressam & explicitam cognitionem habeat. Quanquam enim doceant, respectu multorum fidei dogmatum, privatis sufficere generalem quandam & implicitam fidem, nihilominus requirunt in fidelibus singulis, tanquam ad salutem necessariam, cognitionem aliquam expressam & explicitam primorum saltem & praecipuorum fidei articulorum, cujus generis sunt qui Apostolorum Symbolo continentur. Licet cognitio illa quamvis explicita sit, rudis tamen adhuc & confusa maneat.
pass_a_gloss: They also freely concede that it does not suffice for salvation that someone generally and implicitly believe what the Church believes, even if he has no express and explicit cognition of any of the divine mysteries. For although they teach that, with respect to many dogmas of faith, a certain general and implicit faith suffices for private persons, nevertheless they require in each of the faithful, as necessary for salvation, some express and explicit cognition of at least the first and principal articles of faith, of the kind contained in the Apostles Creed. Even if that cognition is explicit, it may still remain rude and confused.
pass_b_english: Rome concedes that merely believing in general what the Church believes, with no explicit grasp of any mystery, does not suffice for salvation.
Private persons may hold many dogmas only implicitly, but each believer needs some express explicit cognition of at least the principal Creed articles; that cognition may still be rude and confused.

choices.why: Limited to non-principal articles for private persons.
rejected: purely implicit faith of all articles for salvation
